payload.hypothesis: Fixed compliance cost may exclude small competitors.
payload.failureMode: Incumbents may bear greater cost; entry need not decline.

payload.hypothesis: Subsidized downstream demand may transfer rent to a constrained supplier.
payload.failureMode: Supply expansion or buyer bargaining can eliminate margins.

payload.hypothesis: Domestic-content rules may favor approved domestic capacity.
payload.failureMode: Exemptions, imports and added costs may offset protection.

payload.hypothesis: Export restrictions may stimulate a substitute ecosystem.
payload.failureMode: Substitutes may lack technology and users may lose capability.

payload.hypothesis: Procurement expansion may create supplier backlog and pricing power.
payload.failureMode: Cost overruns, fixed-price contracts and delivery failures can destroy returns.

payload.hypothesis: Standards may favor certified incumbents or IP owners.
payload.failureMode: Open standards, substitution and new certifications can erode advantage.

payload.hypothesis: Safety or environmental standards may require replacement spending.
payload.failureMode: Compliance may be deferred and costs may exceed new demand.

payload.hypothesis: Grid-security mandates may favor scarce equipment.
payload.failureMode: Procurement delays and new capacity may erase scarcity.

payload.hypothesis: Tariffs may transfer value upstream from manufacturers to protected inputs.
payload.failureMode: Retaliation and downstream losses may exceed upstream gains.

payload.hypothesis: Reimbursement may expand volume but shift rent to another layer.
payload.failureMode: Volume is not margin or owner cash.

payload.hypothesis: High capital requirements may favor financed incumbents.
payload.failureMode: A funded incumbent can still fail economically.

payload.hypothesis: Deregulation may transfer value from incumbent restrictions to lower-cost entry.
payload.failureMode: Physical bottlenecks can preserve concentration despite legal entry.

payload.hypothesis: Public funding may induce capacity growth followed by competed-away returns.
payload.failureMode: Demand can outgrow capacity; failure is not automatic.

payload.hypothesis: Policy-induced input scarcity may transfer rent upstream.
payload.failureMode: Input substitution and new investment can remove scarcity.

payload.hypothesis: Certification requirements may create recurring compliance demand.
payload.failureMode: Suspension, self-assessment and public tools may reduce paid demand.
